name: Brookfield Asset Management
monetization: Global infrastructure and renewables manager; monetizes AI through the power leg of the buildout — co-owner of Westinghouse with an $80B US-government nuclear partnership — plus data-center platforms, frontier-lab equity (Anthropic), and Nvidia's financing coalition.
description_md: Brookfield is one of the world's largest infrastructure investors, spanning renewables, nuclear (Westinghouse, co-owned ~51% by Brookfield-managed vehicles with Cameco at 49%), data centers, and private credit. Its AI positioning is energy-first: it owns the reactor OEM that the US government has chosen for its AI-era nuclear expansion, and it has pledged large AI-infrastructure programs in Europe (including a reported ~€20B commitment in France).
ai_monetization_md: AI-exposure thesis: AI demand is ultimately a power problem, and Brookfield owns the scarce power assets. Centerpiece: the Oct 2025 strategic partnership under which the US government will arrange financing and permitting for at least $80B of new Westinghouse AP1000/AP300 reactors — with the government earning a participation interest (20% of cash distributions above $17.5B) once vested. Alongside: data-center and renewables platforms contracted to hyperscalers, a participation in Anthropic's $65B Series H (May 2026, amount undisclosed), and founding membership in Nvidia's >$500B compute-collateralized customer-financing coalition (Aug 2026, subject to final agreements).
risk_notes_md: Nuclear construction risk is historically severe (the AP1000's Vogtle precedent ran years late and billions over); the $80B figure is a partnership target, not contracted backlog — final investment decisions rest with the US government. Coalition membership would add GPU-collateralized credit exposure correlated with the same AI cycle driving its power demand thesis.
